newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares fall 3.6 pct on sagging Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares fall 3.6 pct on sagging Dow.

text.p: Brazilian stocks were down 3.6 percent at midafternoon Friday as local prices tracked sharp declines on Wall Street on concerns about U.S. interest rates and the strength of the dollar, brokers said.
"The world scenario is making the bolsa here fall," said a dealer at local Misasi brokerage. Speculation ahead of Monday's options expiration also helped lower shares, he said.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 leading shares was down more than 400 points to 11,476 at 1500 local/1800 GMT on volume of 466.9 million reais ($432.3 million).
Brokers said the steep drops in New York and speculation on options, particularly on the price of benchmark Telebras, drove the local bourse down, albeit in weak trade.
"There is a lot of speculation on the 135-real strike price for Telebras," one dealer said.
Telebras preferred fell 4.47 percent to 139 reais while its common dropped 5.2 percent to 124.50 reais. Telebras regularly accounts for 60 percent of total trade in Sao Paulo.
Power sector shares also dropped, with the Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid power stocks off 2.81 percent at 3,354.
The drop in electrical shares was led by federal power holding Eletrobras'. Its blue-chip preferred B share declined 4.51 percent to 550 reais.
